title: Determine whether a bot can have concurrent turns in flight
description:
## Question

**Can one bot have two turns in flight at once?**

For example a routine wake-up firing while a user turn is live.

This is an **open question in `chatticus-fbae4e`** and it is answerable by reading the scheduler, not by running an experiment. Recorded so it gets read rather than assumed.

## Why it matters

Under the EFS design it no longer threatens correctness — NFS arbitrates concurrent writers, which is the entire point of D3. But it still decides:

- Whether two turns can sensibly **share one working tree**, or whether concurrent turns need separate workspaces
- Whether the workspace scoping proposed in the initiative (`workspace_id` as a first-class noun, default one per bot) is sufficient, or whether the default needs to be finer
- What `hydrate_required` means during the transition period, while the snapshot path is still the running implementation

## Where to look

- `python/src/chatticus/` — the in-memory scheduler
- `features/turn_attempts.feature` — "one request never becomes two answers or two bills from concurrent model calls" suggests turn-level deduplication exists; whether that extends to *bot*-level serialization is the actual question
- `features/single_computer_start.feature` — "concurrent bots share one computer start" establishes that concurrent *bots* share a computer, which is a different question from one bot's concurrent turns

## Cost

Reading, not building.

## Done when

The answer is recorded in `chatticus-fbae4e`'s open questions, with the scoping consequence stated either way.

comments.author: home
comments.text:
**Answer: Yes.** One bot can have multiple turns in flight. There is no bot-level serialization in `enqueue_turn` / `_start_turn_for_bot`; `pending_jobs_for_bot` and `complete_pending_for_bot` handle multiple jobs per bot.

**Turn-attempt dedup is separate:** `turn_attempts.feature` fences duplicate delivery of one logical enqueue per `turn_id`, not one turn per bot.

**Same-channel nuance:** Two ACTIVE turns on one channel are allowed; the active-turn pointer is per-channel and shows only the latest (`_sync_active_channel_turn`).

**Recorded on fbae4e** with `workspace_id` and `hydrate_required` scoping consequences.

Worktree: `/tmp/chatticus-766c51-concurrent-turns` on `spike/concurrent-turns-766c51` (leave until issue closed).

comments.author: home
comments.text:
## Learnings

- **Turns are not serialized per bot.** Admission (`enqueue_turn` / `_start_turn_for_bot`) always creates another turn. `turn_attempts.feature` only fences duplicate *delivery* of one `turn_id`.
- One bot, two channels, two actives is already in `messages.feature`. Same channel can hold two ACTIVE turns; the pointer API shows only the latest.
- **Do not treat "one workspace per bot" as a lock.** Concurrent turns must declare `workspace_id` (or an explicit share policy) if they need an exclusive tree. Under EFS, NFS locking is the writer arbitration; workspace scope is the product isolation boundary.
- `hydrate_required` is a computer/org transition gate, not a bot mutex. It goes away when snapshots go away (D3).
- Routine wake-up during a live user turn is allowed by today's admission path even though routines are not fully wired.
